items.title: Post-incident action items don’t deserve special treatment
items.blurb: Post-incident action items (even those marked P0) often sit untouched for months. Here's why that happens, and how to fix it: better problem statements, the team's regular backlog, and a written record when an item gets deferred.

items.title: The Titanic didn’t sink for just one reason
items.blurb: Why Root Cause Analysis and the Five Whys stop short, told through the Titanic disaster, and what a contributing-factors approach to incidents reveals.

items.title: How to Survive Database Failover – Debezium and PostgreSQL in Production
items.blurb: How to keep Debezium streaming safely through PostgreSQL 16 failover with Patroni 3.3.1 by aligning logical replication slots and Kafka Connect offsets.

items.title: Non-Determinism and Overcount on Modern Hardware Performance Counter Implementations
items.blurb: Abstract: Ideal hardware performance counters provide exact deterministic results. Real-world performance monitoring unit (PMU) implementations do not always live up to this ideal.

items.title: The Thin Orchestrator: How We Made Our AI Agents More Reliable by Giving the Router Less to Do

items.title: We gave cloud agents a phone to QA
items.blurb: Our cloud agents now test mobile pull requests on cloud simulators and leave screenshots and a recording behind. The agent collects the evidence and a person decides whether the change is right.
